attempted_axis: Full body-shape reconstruction pass (work_claim.gamemain-reconstruction.20260831.v1): decoded the complete target disassembly instruction-by-instruction, identified a missing 8-byte stack-frame allocation, a mis-modeled constant-reload site, and reused tier/speed-calc temporaries that should be distinct locals, then bulk-converted ~50 raw u8*+offset accesses to named Enemy/E_ATTRIBUTES struct fields via one declared-once `Enemy* enemy = (Enemy*)e;` alias.

axis_log: Frame-size gap (STRUCTURAL, SUCCEEDED): target reserves 8 more local-area stack bytes than the pre-edit source (0x28 vs 0x20 frame) despite zero stack-relative loads/stores in either stream -- a classic 'declared-but-fully-register-promoted locals still size the frame' MWCC tell (claim.law.mwcc-codegen-tells' pad-array note). Adding `u8 unused[8];` immediately matched the frame exactly and dropped real 242->232 with zero opcode-shape change elsewhere. Declaration POSITION of the pad (first local vs last local) and TYPE (u8[8] vs two separate s32 scalars) were both A/B'd and are neutral -- only the total declared byte footprint matters.

Stale-vs-fresh constant reload (SUCCEEDED): target reloads lbl_80346820 fresh via a dedicated lfs immediately before the e+776/e+772 pair (register f0), while the pre-edit source reused the long-lived z2 local (already resident since much earlier) -- a real semantic difference in operand liveness, not just a naming choice. Routing that ONE pair through the existing 'fv' scratch local (`fv = lbl_80346820; ...; = fv;`) reproduced the single fresh lfs reused for both stores exactly; writing the global literal directly at both sites instead (no local) cost 2 instructions (each site independently reloaded) and was reverted first.

hi/lo/t split into hi2/lo2/t2 (NEUTRAL, KEPT for reconstruction quality): the tier-calc block (scale vs health-derived thresholds) and the later speed-calc block (ht vs speed-derived thresholds) shared one hi/lo/t triple across two register lifetimes target keeps fully disjoint (no live-range overlap, separated by a format_brain() call). Splitting into a second named triple is real-count-neutral (replaces the abstract 8-byte pad exactly, same compiled bytes) but is a materially more honest reconstruction than an inert padding array, so it was kept in place of the pad.

Table-access single-additive form (FAILED, reverted): rewriting the 6 SoA-table sites that compile to addi+lfsx/lwzx (target wants add+lfs/lwz-displacement) from `row = tbl + *(s32*)e*4; ((T*)row)[N]` to one raw expression `*(T*)(tbl + *(s32*)e*4 + CONST)` produced BYTE-IDENTICAL compiled output at every one of the 6 sites (zero opcode change) and, when combined with removing the now-unused 'row' declarations at two adjacent sites, introduced a NEW regression at a previously-clean 7th site (2624/e+192) -- see the companion boundary-refinement law proposed with this record.

One-case switch for the ty==30 skip (FAILED, reverted): target's `bne ->X; b ->join` (2 insns) vs our `beq ->join` (1 insn) at the ht/ty tier-speed guard was hypothesized to reflect a `switch(ty){case 30: break; default: ...}` source shape per claim.law.compare-form-dictionary's one-case-switch note. Compiled to byte-identical output to the existing nested-if form; not the cause.

Compound `&&` condition for the same guard (FAILED, no effect): rewriting `if(!(ht>hi2)){if(ty!=30){...}}` as `if(!(ht>hi2) && ty!=30){...}` compiled identically (as expected -- MWCC treats both as the same IR here).

for-loop vs manual while-loop for the fxhittime zero-fill (FAILED, no effect): converting the `for(i4=0;i4<20;i4+=4)` to an equivalent `i4=0; while(i4<20){...; i4+=4;}` compiled identically; the loop's induction-register choice (target reuses the register freed by the dead slot*916 mulli temp; ours allocates a fresh one, the source of 2 of the remaining structural diffs) is not controlled by loop-statement AST shape.

Padding TYPE (u8[8] vs 2x s32 scalar) (FAILED to differentiate, confirms size-only sensitivity): both forms produced byte-identical compiled output once the hi2/lo2/t2 split subsumed the padding role.
